_comment: Shared AWS infrastructure pricing rates (us-east-1, USD) for the estimate phase. Rates evolve on AWS's cadence, independent of the cost algorithm, so they live here as DATA and the estimate procedure does a lookup, not a guess. Each service carries its rates + a multi_az_handling key; the cost FORMULAS live in the estimate phase's prose (the algorithm is not data). Consumed by the heroku-to-aws and azure-to-aws skills; intended to be shared with gcp-to-aws, which still has its own markdown cache. AI-model / DynamoDB / Redshift / Athena / SageMaker rates are NOT here (they remain in the gcp-to-aws pricing cache). Lambda WAS on that exclusion list and no longer is — azure-to-aws maps consumption-plan Function Apps to Lambda, so the rates were harvested here from gcp's cache.
_region_warning: EVERY rate in this file is _meta.region (us-east-1) and there is no multiplier. A design targeting another region is being priced with us-east-1 numbers: eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 run roughly 5-12% higher for compute and RDS, and some services differ more. This file cannot fix that on its own — the consuming estimate MUST compare the design's target region against _meta.region and, when they differ, either reprice via the awspricing MCP (which takes a region parameter; note .mcp.json pins AWS_REGION=us-east-1 as the SERVER default, so the region must be passed per call) or state the mismatch next to every total and widen the accuracy band. Silently presenting us-east-1 figures as a eu-west-1 estimate is the failure this key exists to prevent.

_meta.staleness_note: If more than staleness_days past last_updated, infrastructure rates remain reliable; set pricing_source=cached_stale and note it. AI-model rates (not used for heroku->aws) may have drifted.

Aurora PostgreSQL: r6g family re-verified (rates decreased); db.r6g.12xlarge added; db.r6g.16xlarge now directly confirmed. ElastiCache: m6g family all sizes directly confirmed from API (major decreases replacing prior extrapolations). EC2: r6i family corrected (was ~20% too high); t4g and m6g slightly updated. EKS r6i node_rates_monthly recomputed from confirmed EC2 r6i rates. _multi_az_convention._comment: THE TRAP: a design's multi_az:true means different things per service. Each service rate below carries multi_az_handling so the formula applies the RIGHT adjustment, never a blanket multiplier.
_multi_az_convention.baked_in: rate already INCLUDES multi-AZ; NEVER apply a multiplier (multi_az flag is informational)
_multi_az_convention.multiplier_x2: rate is single-AZ; multiply by 2 when design multi_az == true
_multi_az_convention.intrinsic: service is inherently multi-AZ; no adjustment; multi_az flag informational

fargate.multi_az_handling: n/a (Fargate cost is task-size driven, not AZ-driven)

alb._note: monthly_fixed confirmed 2026-09-29: $0.0225/ALB-hr × 730 hrs = $16.425 ≈ 16.43 (AmazonEC2 LoadBalancerUsage). per_lcu_hour UNVERIFIED — USE1-LCUUsage query returned empty; existing cached rate preserved.

nlb._note: Network Load Balancer: monthly_fixed confirmed 2026-09-29 ($0.0225/NLB-hr × 730 = 16.43, same fixed charge as ALB, AmazonEC2 LoadBalancerUsage). per_lcu_hour UNVERIFIED — USE1-LCUUsage query returned empty; existing cached rate preserved. Priced by the same formula shape as alb.

rds_postgresql._note: RDS PostgreSQL Multi-AZ on-demand hourly, us-east-1. Rate ALREADY includes multi-AZ — do NOT double for multi_az. All rows re-verified 2026-09-29 via AWS Pricing API (AmazonRDS, deploymentOption=Multi-AZ, databaseEngine=PostgreSQL). m6g family decreased ~11%; r6g family slightly decreased; t3 small-xlarge increased ~6%; r6i family increased ~4%; x2g.16xlarge increased significantly. db.m6g.12xlarge, db.t3.micro, db.t3.2xlarge added as new confirmed rows.
rds_postgresql._instances_note: Multi-AZ on-demand hourly, us-east-1. All families re-verified 2026-09-29 via AWS Pricing API. t4g.* for dev/small workloads; m6g/r6g (Graviton) and m6i/r6i (x86) for production; x2g.16xlarge for very large memory workloads. x86 rows are the azure default for Windows/.NET fleets; Graviton is lower cost for equivalent sizes. Every rds_instance_class the design can emit MUST have a rate here (no unpriced production DBs).

aurora_postgresql._note: Aurora replicates across 3 AZs by default; rate is as-listed, no multi-AZ adjustment. All rows re-verified 2026-09-29 via AWS Pricing API (AmazonRDS, deploymentOption=Single-AZ, databaseEngine=Aurora PostgreSQL). r6g family decreased ~6-7% vs prior cache. db.r6g.12xlarge added; db.r6g.16xlarge now directly confirmed from API (was previously extrapolated).
aurora_postgresql._instances_note: Single-AZ on-demand hourly per instance (reader nodes priced separately), us-east-1. All rows confirmed 2026-09-29 via AWS Pricing API.

elasticache._note: ElastiCache Redis Single-AZ on-demand; apply x2 when design multi_az == true. All rows re-verified 2026-09-29 via AWS Pricing API. m6g family decreased ~28% vs prior cache (all sizes now directly confirmed from API, replacing prior extrapolations).
elasticache._nodes_note: Redis (OSS) on-demand rates, us-east-1. t4g/t3 for dev/small workloads; m6g for production. All m6g sizes confirmed directly from AWS Pricing API 2026-09-29.

msk._note: broker_count already spans AZs (2 or 3 per design); cost is per-broker, no extra multi-AZ multiplier. Rates confirmed unchanged 2026-09-29 via AWS Pricing API (AmazonMSK).
msk._brokers_note: MSK broker rates, us-east-1. t3.small, m5.large, m5.2xlarge, m5.12xlarge confirmed via AWS Pricing API 2026-09-29; m5.xlarge/4xlarge/8xlarge scale linearly and match expected ladder.

ebs._default_note: eb_root_volume_gb_default is the AL2023 EB default root size; use aws_config.root_volume_gb when the design specifies one.

Existing cached rates preserved. Azure Service Bus queues / Storage Queues map to SQS. Standard $0.40/M requests, FIFO $0.50/M; 1M requests/mo free tier (not subtracted).

sns._note: per_million_publishes confirmed $0.50/M via AWS Pricing API 2026-09-29 (AmazonSNS). Azure Event Grid / Service Bus topics map to SNS. SQS delivery $0.00/M; HTTP delivery $0.60/M; 1M publishes/mo free tier.

fast_path_services._comment: Flat monthly_baseline_est per fast-path add-on — PINNED stated assumptions for the stopgap (these are estimates, not measured rates; an external pricing source will replace them). per-unit rates kept as documentation of the basis. Use monthly_baseline_est as the breakdown mid; mark the line as an estimate.

s3._basis: assumes ~50GB + light requests; storage_per_gb_month is the rate basis

ses._basis: assumes <50k emails/mo @ per_1000_emails; flat placeholder pending usage data

secrets_manager._basis: assumes ~3 secrets @ per_secret_month + light API calls; per_secret_month confirmed $0.40 via AWS Pricing API 2026-09-29

elasticache_memcached._use: same node rates as elasticache (Memcachier mapping)

cloudwatch._note: standard_alarm_month ($0.10) and custom_metric_month ($0.30) confirmed unchanged via AWS Pricing API 2026-09-29 (AmazonCloudWatch). xray_per_million_traces UNVERIFIED — API returns XRay Spans Indexed at $0.00000075/span which does not map cleanly to the cached $5/million-traces rate; existing rate preserved pending clarification.

ec2._comment: EC2 On-Demand hourly rates (Linux/x86 unless noted as Graviton, us-east-1). Used by the Elastic Beanstalk cost formula to price underlying instances. Every instance_type the EB design can emit MUST have a rate here.
ec2._instances_note: On-demand Linux rates, us-east-1. Re-verified 2026-09-29 via AWS Pricing API. t4g family updated (minor increases); m6g family updated (minor increases); r6i family corrected (was ~20% too high in prior cache — e.g. r6i.large was $0.1512, now confirmed $0.126). m6i, c6i, r6g, m7g, c7g confirmed unchanged. Graviton (t4g, m6g, r6g, m7g, c7g) rates ~15-20% below x86 counterparts.
ec2._m6i_note: m6i/c6i/r6i/m7g/c7g size ladders present to cover the instance types the design sizing tables (vm-ec2-sizing.json, appservice-eb-sizing.json) can emit, at published us-east-1 Linux on-demand rates. Verify via the awspricing MCP for large estimates.
ec2._windows_note: THESE RATES ARE LINUX. An instance whose design carries license_model 'License Included' (Windows Server, SQL Server) costs materially MORE than the row above — roughly 2x for a general-purpose size — and no Windows rate or per-vCPU license adder is in this file. Pricing a Windows instance from a Linux row understates it, in the direction that flatters AWS and can invert a migrate/stay recommendation. Look the Windows rate up via the awspricing MCP (AmazonEC2, operatingSystem=Windows, preInstalledSw=NA); when the MCP is unreachable, label the line per the estimate phase's partial-line rule rather than silently using the Linux number.

lambda._comment: AWS Lambda rates (us-east-1). per_request confirmed unchanged 2026-09-29 via AWS Pricing API. Azure Function Apps on a consumption plan map to Lambda.
lambda._no_invocation_data_note: Lambda cost is invocation-driven, and IaC declares no invocation count. With no measured request volume there is no figure to compute: emit null with a stated reason rather than a remembered default. A source consumption plan provisions no worker capacity, so there is no source-side number to carry across either.

_rate_row_coverage._comment: THE GAP CLASS this file kept hitting: a service can be present here while the specific RATE ROW a design needs is absent. 'ec2' is in the file; a design emitting m6i.2xlarge finds no row. The shared pricing-mode.md hierarchy keyed its first rung on SERVICE presence, so that case fell through labeled 'cached' with no number behind it. Rung 1b in pricing-mode.md now covers it.
_rate_row_coverage._who_owes_what: A skill's sizing tables and this file are a PAIR: every instance_type/instance_class/node_type a sizing table can emit needs a row here, or the estimate has a hole. The pair is not enforced by any tool today. heroku never diverged because its sizing table and these rates were co-authored; a skill whose sizing tables were written from source-cloud SKUs will diverge on day one.
_rate_row_coverage._do_not_paper_over: Do NOT substitute a neighbouring row for a missing one (an m5 rate for an m6i design, an rds_postgresql row for a DocumentDB class). A near-miss rate is indistinguishable from a correct one in the output and is never caught. Query the MCP, or mark the line unpriced.

_absent_services._comment: Services a consuming skill's design can emit that have NO rates here or in the gcp-to-aws pricing cache. Listed so the hole is visible in the data rather than discovered mid-estimate. Each needs an awspricing MCP lookup; until then the estimate marks the line unavailable and excludes it from totals. NEVER fabricate a rate for one of these.
_absent_services.documentdb: Azure Cosmos DB (Mongo API) maps to DocumentDB. No documentdb section exists. db.t3.medium is a DOCUMENTDB instance class here — do not read it from rds_postgresql.instances: different service, and those rates are baked-in Multi-AZ. MCP: AmazonDocDB.
_absent_services.fsx_windows: Azure Files (SMB) maps to FSx for Windows File Server. No fsx section exists. Needs per-GiB-month SSD/HDD, single-AZ vs multi-AZ, and throughput capacity. MCP: AmazonFSx.
_absent_services.ec2_windows_license: See ec2._windows_note. MCP: AmazonEC2 with operatingSystem=Windows.
_absent_services.ecr: Azure Container Registry maps to Amazon ECR. No ecr rates here or in the gcp-to-aws pricing cache. Needs per-GB-month storage + data-transfer rates. Surface it as a visible excluded line rather than pricing it silently. MCP: AmazonECR.
_absent_services.dynamodb: Azure Cosmos DB (Core/Table API) maps to DynamoDB. No dynamodb rates here. Needs on-demand vs provisioned WCU/RCU + storage. Surface as a visible excluded line; never fabricate. MCP: AmazonDynamoDB.
_absent_services.efs: Azure Files (NFS) maps to EFS. No efs section. Needs per-GiB-month (Standard/IA) + throughput mode. Excluded line until priced. MCP: AmazonEFS.
_absent_services.kinesis: Azure Event Hubs (AMQP/SDK) maps to Kinesis Data Streams. No kinesis rates. Needs shard-hour + PUT payload units (on-demand vs provisioned). Excluded line. MCP: AmazonKinesis.
_absent_services.neptune: Azure Cosmos DB (Gremlin API) maps to Neptune. No neptune rates. Needs instance-hour + I/O + storage. Excluded line. MCP: AmazonNeptune.
_absent_services.keyspaces: Azure Cosmos DB (Cassandra API) maps to Amazon Keyspaces. No keyspaces rates. Needs on-demand/provisioned RU + storage. Excluded line. MCP: AmazonMCS.
_absent_services.backup: Azure Backup / Recovery Services vault maps to AWS Backup. No backup rates. Needs per-GB-month warm/cold storage by resource type. Excluded line. MCP: AWSBackup.
_absent_services.network_firewall: Azure Firewall maps to AWS Network Firewall. No rates. Needs endpoint-hour + per-GB processed. Excluded line. MCP: AWSNetworkFirewall.
_absent_services.appconfig: Azure App Configuration maps to AWS AppConfig. No rates. Needs config-store + API-call pricing. Excluded line. MCP: AWSAppConfig.

_no_cost_services._comment: AWS services a consuming skill's design can emit that carry NO standalone charge (control-plane, IAM, or free-tier resources). Listed so the coverage oracle treats them as intentionally rate-free rather than a missing rate. A service here must be genuinely free of a direct hourly/GB/request charge — costs it INDUCES (e.g. NAT for a VPC, data transfer) are priced on their own lines.
_no_cost_services.vpc: A VPC itself is free; NAT gateway, data transfer, endpoints are separate priced lines.
_no_cost_services.vpc_peering: No hourly charge; cross-AZ/region data transfer is a separate concern.
_no_cost_services.kms_key: A customer-managed KMS key is ~$1/mo but is bundled into the security baseline, not a per-design line; treated as no standalone design cost here.
_no_cost_services.route53_routing_policy: A routing policy is a config of a hosted zone (route53 is priced); no separate charge.
_no_cost_services.session_manager: Systems Manager Session Manager (Azure Bastion target) has no per-hour charge — the deliberate cost win over an EC2 bastion.
_no_cost_services.ami: An AMI itself has no charge beyond the EBS snapshot backing it (ebs snapshot is a separate concern).
